task_class: Rust repository feature implementation when local Rust execution is unavailable or unreliable
evidence: Multiple slices produced intentional compile or test RED failures followed by green fmt, clippy, build, and workspace tests
Final exact-head CI run 417 passed all jobs including the historical corpus smoke
strengths: Preserves executable RED/GREEN evidence without a local toolchain
Separates semantic failures from formatting and lint noise
Prevents stale-run completion claims when exact head is enforced
failure_modes: Feedback is slower than local execution
Formatting-only failures can obscure the intended RED signal
Stale CI runs can be mistaken for current evidence without exact-head checks
when_to_use: Remote-access repository work where CI is authoritative and local build tooling is absent
when_not_to_use: Tight inner-loop development when a working local toolchain is available
better_alternative: Use a local TDD loop first when available, then exact-head CI as the independent gate
environment_constraints: Rust stable 1.97.1 in the final run

evidence: A descendant retaining inherited pipes reproduced an approximately 20.03 second hang after direct-child kill
An early-exiting leader with a surviving descendant reproduced an approximately 20.01 second hang
Process-group plus leader-and-capture deadline supervision passed the complete Rust workspace tests
strengths: Finds lifecycle defects normal happy-path tests miss
Turns security review findings into executable invariants
failure_modes: Unix behavior does not directly generalize to Windows
when_to_use: Timeouts, process trees, pipes, daemon children, cancellation, shell or tool runners, and CI executors
when_not_to_use: Pure in-process functions with no external lifecycle

task_class: Trustworthy evaluation infrastructure for autonomous software development
combination: same verifier on base and accepted revisions
evidence: The full historical smoke passed with all five base/reference distinctions in 260.53 seconds on final CI
strengths: Provides an empirical control condition for AutoDev improvements
Makes future context, routing, planning, and repair changes measurable
failure_modes: Historical environment and toolchain drift can invalidate fixtures
The complete smoke is relatively expensive
A poorly designed fixture can test infrastructure absence instead of behavior
when_to_use: Evaluating agent, planner, context, routing, repair, or self-improvement changes
when_not_to_use: Tiny deterministic library refactors already fully specified by local tests
environment_constraints: Historical verifier dependencies must remain obtainable

task_class: Reconciling a long-running feature branch with concurrently merged mainline architecture
evidence: Feature divergence moved from seven commits behind to zero
Only Cargo.lock and crates/forge-core/src/lib.rs overlapped the concurrent PR surface
The reconciled branch became mergeable and passed the full CI suite
strengths: Avoids replaying dozens of feature commits
failure_modes: Lockfile and export reconciliation still require focused review
Pre-merge green CI is invalid after reconciliation
when_to_use: Large feature branches where current main changed in adjacent but mostly non-overlapping areas
when_not_to_use: Small branches where a normal rebase is trivial and locally verifiable

task_class: Rust workspace lockfile repair after adding a workspace member
context: Self-Evaluation Factory v0 combined with concurrently evolved main dependencies
combination: normal workspace resolution from the existing lock
evidence: cargo generate-lockfile caused unrelated futures, ICU, rmcp, and other upgrades
Resolving from main's existing lock produced only the new autodev-eval package stanza
The resulting workspace passed cargo check --locked and final CI
strengths: Makes lockfile review small and causal
Catches silently mutable lockfiles in CI
failure_modes: A genuinely incompatible existing lock can still require transitive resolution changes
when_to_use: Adding crates or workspace members when the dependency graph should otherwise remain stable
when_not_to_use: Intentional dependency refresh or upgrade work
failed_strategy: Using cargo generate-lockfile as the first repair step for a minimal-diff feature branch

task_class: Temporary CI-assisted deterministic repository mutation when local tooling is unavailable
context: Formatter and lockfile repair attempts during Self-Evaluation Factory v0
evidence: A one-shot formatter successfully produced canonical rustfmt changes
A lockfile finalizer that attempted to push a commit modifying ci.yml was blocked by GitHub token workflow-write restrictions
strengths: Can obtain canonical formatter or lockfile artifacts when local tooling is absent
failure_modes: Temporary workflow residue can expand authority if not removed
Adds noisy commits and operational complexity
when_to_use: Only deterministic formatter or lockfile artifacts when no local execution path exists and connector writes cannot reproduce canonical output
when_not_to_use: Any case where normal local execution or read-only CI verification is available
better_alternative: Prefer a local toolchain or read-only CI; if mutation is unavoidable constrain the workflow to one deterministic artifact and delete it immediately
